name: veterinary_clinic_system_079_appointment_to_visit_linkage
instruction: Run the appointment-to-visit follow-through audit. A completed appointment is clinically closed only when a visit_records row exists with the exact same patient_id, provider_id, and a visit_date whose calendar day equals the appointment's appointment_date calendar day. (1) Read the live appointments and visit_records; identify which completed appointments already have a matching seed visit record and do not create duplicates for those. (2) For every other completed appointment, create a minimal visit_records row with the same patient_id, provider_id, location_id, visit_date, weight_kg copied from the patient, generated_from set to the appointment id, and a subjective note that includes the appointment id. (3) Write one ops_reports row {report: 'follow_through', batch_code, completed_appointments, already_matched, generated, matched, unmatched, match_pct, unmatched_ids, generated_ids}. unmatched_ids must be the ascending comma-joined ids of any unmatched completed appointments (empty string if none), and generated_ids must be the ascending comma-joined ids of all generated appointments. Delete any prior follow_through row for this batch before writing. The verifier checks every seed visit_record row is unchanged, that every new visit row has a unique generated_from pointing to a completed appointment with a matching triple, and that all counts are re-derived both from raw rows and from SQL.
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session
_max_steps_note: set to par_steps * 1.5 after live measurement

success_criteria.summary: Identify the one completed appointment that already matches a seed visit_record by exact triple (patient_id, provider_id, calendar-day date). Create one new visit_record for each of the remaining completed appointments with generated_from set to the appointment id and matching triple. Write one ops_reports follow_through row with the exact counts and id lists. Verifier canaries every other collection, asserts each new visit row identity, and recomputes counts via raw rows and SQL.

checks.expect: 175 new visit rows, one per completed appointment that lacks a matching seed visit, each with generated_from = appointment id and triple matching the appointment
exactly one follow_through row for the batch with completed, already_matched, generated, matched, unmatched, match_pct, unmatched_ids, generated_ids
completed count and matched count agree between raw-row Python and SQL join; new-visit and pre-existing counts agree between raw-row set identity and SQL id-threshold joins

hazards: Pre-existing match: completed appointment id 486 (patient_id 30, provider_id 3, appointment_date 2026-08-29) matches seed visit_record id 164 with the same triple. A solution that creates a new visit_record for every completed appointment (including this one) over-reports generated and under-reports already_matched.

Duplicate completed triples: appointment ids 150 and 378 both have (patient_id 67, provider_id 3, appointment_date 2026-08-19); ids 154 and 155 both have (patient_id 61, provider_id 3, appointment_date 2026-08-05). Two completed appointments can share the same triple, so a solution that creates one visit per unique triple produces 174 records and fails the new-visit count and generated_ids set equality.

Decoy seed visits: there are 371 seed visit_records (ids 1..371) and only one matches a completed appointment. Every other seed visit must survive byte-identical. Any update, deletion, or addition of generated_from to a seed row is caught by the row-level canary and the generated_from set check.

Partial-match traps: matching on patient_id only or on visit_date only over-matches and creates either too few or too many visit records. The verifier requires an exact triple match and a generated_from value equal to a real completed appointment id.

No-visit 100% report: an agent may write a follow_through row claiming match_pct=100.0 and empty unmatched_ids without creating the visit records. The verifier's SQL join and row-level generated_from checks require the 175 new visit rows to actually exist.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a reconciliation sweep (find the one completed appointment with a pre-existing seed visit) with a repair pass (generate the missing visit records) and an aggregation/report (follow-through counts and id lists). The task requires exact triple matching, handling duplicate completed-appointment triples, and tracking the source appointment id via generated_from on the generated rows. The verifier uses both row-level set identity and SQL id-threshold joins for dual-path counts, not a single join.
